It solves the memory inefficiency of dense grids by storing only the necessary nodes [S2].

The evidence explicitly states that the proposed data structures (SVOs and PSVOs) are 'Sparse Voxel Octrees' designed for scenes where the proportion of active voxels is low (e.g., 0.01%). It details how the structure recursively decomposes the grid and creates child nodes only for 'active' child octants, while passive octants are marked with a 0 bit and no further nodes are created for them. This mechanism inherently stores only the necessary nodes (those representing active geometry) rather than a dense grid of all possible voxels, thereby solving the memory inefficiency associated with dense grids.

Pointerless Sparse Voxel Octrees (PSVO) are a variant where the relationship between a parent node's child hint (HT) and its associated child node is expressed by the location of the binary representation of the child node immediately after the binary representation of the corresponding HT of the parent node, without using pointers [S2].
